page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 2 vCPUs, 1 physical core across 2 threads, and 16.0 GB of memory. It runs on x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC 7B13 processors equipped with 32 MB L3 cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. The instance features dedicated CPU allocation and supports instruction extensions including AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, FMA, and BMI2, though it lacks AVX-512 support. Local storage is omitted, and no GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are attached.

Benchmark testing indicates a distinct separation between single-core and multi-threaded performance. Single-core processing is strong, ranking in the top tier of stress-ng CPU tests alongside average single-threaded compression and text processing results. However, total multi-core execution and memory bandwidth are limited by the single physical core layout, placing multi-core Geekbench, software compilation, and Redis throughput in lower performance brackets. Qualitatively, the high RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers efficient resource utilization for applications needing elevated memory capacity without requiring extra compute overhead.

With its 8 GB RAM per vCPU profile, n2d-highmem-2 fits memory-intensive tasks with low concurrency needs. Recommended applications include lightweight in-memory caching services, background queue workers, text manipulation routines, and web microservices demanding moderate operational memory footprints.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized x86_64 instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core on AMD EPYC 7B13 processors, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM. Designed with an 8 GB memory-per-core ratio, the server provides 32 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets while omitting local SSD storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU execution, achieving competitive stress-ng single-threaded scores and balanced text processing. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput, memory bandwidth, and compilation speed reflect the physical single-core limit. Qualitatively, n2d-highmem-2 provides cost efficiency by delivering ample RAM capacity for memory-bound tasks without forcing scale-up of compute resources. It is best suited for small in-memory caches, background queue processing, single-threaded data manipulation, and lightweight microservices requiring elevated RAM allocations.
